children: The acquisition will give Nvidia access to 'one of the most important parcels of real estate in the AI market' and promote open-source technology
Nvidia on Thursday announced a deal to buy Hugging Face, a repository for open-source artificial-intelligence models that has been growing in stature in recent years.
Nvidia (NVDA) will pay roughly $11.9 billion to Hugging Face shareholders and $1.0 billion to Hugging Face employees who will join the chip giant.

The transaction will give Nvidia access to what D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria called "one of the most important parcels of real estate in the AI market." Hugging Face specifically serves as a place where AI developers can share models, weightings, data sets and other information that allows them to build in a collaborative way.
Luria said Hugging Face reminds him of GitHub, a platform where people share code. Microsoft (MSFT) acquired it back in 2018.

"One of the learnings from the GitHub acquisition is that allowing a large integrated platform to acquire an important repository puts everybody else at a disadvantage," he wrote in a note to clients earlier this week.

Once the deal closes - it is expected to happen in the first half of next year - Nvidia will have an expanded footprint in the world of open-source AI, which has been gaining popularity lately as developers look for cheaper ways to build.
Nvidia shares were down fractionally in premarket action on Thursday. Reports last week said the deal was done, making it somewhat anticipated to investors.

In a Thursday blog post, Nvidia touted open-source models as a way of making AI technology more accessible. "Open models let startups, businesses, universities and public institutions build on advanced capabilities without training every model from scratch," the company said.
Hugging Face fetched a private-market valuation of $4.5 billion back in 2023.
